issues.legal_issue: A statutory provision preserving pre-existing contracts for enforcement by a successor corporation does not deem those contracts to have been originally entered into by the corporation.
material_facts: The borrowers had executed mortgages in favour of insurance companies before the successor corporation was established.
After taking over the insurers’ life insurance business, the corporation sued to recover the mortgage debts.
The contracts were subsisting immediately before the transfer of the insurers’ business.
issues.conclusion: The provision did not create a legal fiction that the corporation had been the original party to the contracts; it enabled the corporation to enforce them after the transfer.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(1) of the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956, provided for subsisting contracts and instruments to be enforceable by or against the Corporation after vesting, rather than deeming the Corporation to have been their original party. Section 9(2), which permitted pending proceedings to continue by or against the Corporation, supported that construction. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.recovery_suit_by_successor_corporation: A successor corporation sued to enforce a contract taken over from another entity.
predicates.preexisting_contract_transferred: The contract was made by the predecessor before its business was transferred to the successor.
predicates.contract_subsisting_at_transfer: The contract remained in force immediately before the transfer of the predecessor’s business.

issues.definition: When a successor corporation sues on a transferred contract that was made by its predecessor and remained in force at transfer, the contract is not treated as having been originally made by the successor.

issues.legal_issue: A successor corporation recovering a transferred debt remains subject to a debt-reduction obligation that attached to the debt before the transfer.
material_facts: Agriculturist borrowers obtained mortgage loans from insurance companies before the successor corporation was established.
The corporation later took over the insurers’ life insurance businesses and sued to recover the mortgage debts.
The borrowers claimed that the debts were subject to reduction under the applicable agriculturists’ relief legislation.
The debt-reduction obligation existed in respect of the debts when the insurers’ assets and liabilities vested in the corporation.
issues.conclusion: The debts remained subject to reduction under the agriculturists’ relief legislation, and the corporation could not rely on the exemption for debts due to a corporation to avoid that obligation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7(1) of the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956 transferred and vested the insurers’ relevant assets and liabilities in the Corporation; section 7(2) included existing debts, liabilities and obligations of whatever kind. Section 9(1) allowed the Corporation to enforce transferred contracts but did not erase obligations attached to them. Section 4(e) of the Madras Agriculturists Relief Act, 1938 excluded specified debts, including debts due to certain corporations, from the Act; it did not remove an obligation to scale down a debt that had attached before transfer. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: recovery_suit_by_successor_corporation and debtor_is_agriculturist and predecessor_created_debt and debt_reduction_obligation_attached_before_transfer and debt_transferred_to_successor

predicates.recovery_suit_by_successor_corporation: A successor corporation sued to recover a debt taken over from another entity.
predicates.debtor_is_agriculturist: The debtor was an agriculturist for purposes of the applicable debt-relief law.
predicates.predecessor_created_debt: The predecessor entity, rather than the successor, originally advanced the loan or otherwise became entitled to the debt.
predicates.debt_reduction_obligation_attached_befor: The debt was subject to a debt-reduction obligation before the predecessor’s relevant business was transferred.
predicates.debt_transferred_to_successor: The predecessor’s debt and associated obligations passed to the successor with the transferred business.

issues.definition: If a successor corporation sues on a transferred debt owed by an agriculturist, and the predecessor created the debt and its reduction obligation attached before transfer, the successor must honor that obligation.
